snp5.12:1.4: Per Nd II, the Buddha is called the Simultaneous Eye because the eye of his omniscience arose at the very moment of his awakening. It seems unlikely Jatukaṇṇin would have that idea in mind on first addressing the Buddha, though — more plausibly he’s alluding to the Buddha’s ability to see and understand things the instant they arise.
snp5.12:4.3: Per Nd II, “before” refers to defilements tied to the past, “after” to defilements tied to the future, and “in between” to the five aggregates — form, feeling, perception, thought-fabrications, and sensory consciousness — in the present.
